selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: After thinking about one spring as a sign, what conclusion did the traveler reach about denying resurrection?
questions.answer: He concluded that rejecting resurrection deserves punishment because it rejects clear proofs, divine promises, and divine power.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is denial of resurrection a serious mistake?
questions.answer: Because it means refusing to accept many promises and doubting the ability of the One who has full power to bring it about.

questions.question: Whose repeated assurances are mentioned as support for resurrection?
questions.answer: The assurances brought through all of the prophets are mentioned.

questions.question: Besides the prophets, what other source is given as repeated evidence for resurrection?
questions.answer: Many verses of the Qur’an, both direct and indirect, are given as evidence.

questions.question: How often does the passage say these assurances were given?
questions.answer: It says they were given many times, described as thousands of times.

questions.question: How is the future resurrection compared with what happens in spring?
questions.answer: It is presented as easier than the many amazing gatherings and renewals that appear every spring.

questions.question: What quality of Allah is emphasized to answer doubts about resurrection?
questions.answer: His irresistible and complete power is emphasized.

questions.question: What other divine quality is stressed alongside power?
questions.answer: Majestic wrath and glory are also stressed, showing that justice is part of the matter.

questions.question: What response came from the nafs after the traveler’s reflection?
questions.answer: It accepted the statement and expressed belief in it.

questions.question: What is the final result of the inner dialogue?
questions.answer: The inner self confirms belief.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the traveler’s inner reflection in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the justice of punishment for those who deny resurrection.

questions.question: On what basis does the traveler call that punishment just?
questions.answer: He sees it as just because denial rejects repeated divine promises and denies divine ability.

questions.question: What two kinds of testimony are mentioned in support of resurrection?
questions.answer: The message of the prophets and the verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: Does the passage present resurrection as difficult or easy for Allah? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents it as easy for Allah, even easier than the repeated wonders seen in spring.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention spring more than once?
questions.answer: To use visible, repeated events in nature as evidence that bringing life back is fully possible.

questions.question: What role do the Qur’anic verses play in the traveler’s reasoning?
questions.answer: They serve as repeated revealed proof that resurrection and gathering will happen.

questions.question: What is significant about the nafs answering back?
questions.answer: It shows an inner struggle ending in submission to the truth.

questions.question: What final attitude is reached by the end of the passage?
questions.answer: An attitude of acceptance and belief.

questions.question: How is the final resurrection ranked in relation to spring renewals?
questions.answer: It is described as easier than those repeated spring wonders.

questions.question: What judgment does he make about people who deny resurrection?
questions.answer: He judges that punishment in Hell is deserved for them.

questions.question: What is one reason he gives for that judgment related to Allah’s words?
questions.answer: Denial goes against many promises given by Allah.

questions.question: What is another reason he gives related to Allah’s ability?
questions.answer: Denial also means refusing to accept the power of the One who can certainly do it.

questions.question: Which messengers are said to have received this promise?
questions.answer: All of the prophets are described as having been assured of it.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an support this teaching according to the passage?
questions.answer: It contains many verses that state or indicate resurrection and gathering.
